title: PARC 3.0: A Corpus of Attribution Relations
task_description: Extract complete attribution relations by identifying and linking source, cue, and content spans across quotation, opinion, fact, belief, direct, indirect, mixed, and nested cases.
inputs: Wall Street Journal/PDTB-derived news text with attribution annotations
outputs_or_labels: Attribution relation plus source/cue/content spans; around 20,000 ARs
artifact_access_status: paper open; dataset available for research use, exact download endpoint not verified
license_status: not stated on opened scholarly page
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states fully annotated ARs, source/cue/content spans, ~20k ARs, research availability; PDF/search evidence reports direct/indirect/mixed and nested AR coverage.
limitations: News genre; source entity resolution and opinion target are identified as desirable future additions; license/download details require follow-up.
why_relevant: Closest general benchmark for claim ownership: explicitly separates source, cue, and content and includes authorial stance-bearing attribution structures.

title: An Attribution Relations Corpus for Political News
authors: Edward Newell; Drew Margolin; Derek Ruths
task_description: Extract attribution relations in political news, including quoted statements and descriptions of internal states such as thoughts and intentions.
inputs: 1,008 US political-news articles from 7 publishers covering the 2016 presidential campaign
outputs_or_labels: Token labels for source, cue, content, or none; ~24,000 attributions; train/dev/test and standoff annotations
pipeline_gap_filled: attributed claims; source ownership; disagreement/stance-bearing political reporting
artifact_access_status: open GitHub repository with data, metadata, standoff annotations, and CoreNLP XML
license_status: repository license not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL metadata verifies paper identity; official repository documents 1,008 articles, 760k words, ~24k attributions, source/cue/content labels, and train/dev/test structure.
limitations: Political-news domain; univocal labels disallow overlapping/nested attributions unlike PARC3; source links are textual annotations rather than a full discourse argument graph.
why_relevant: Strong benchmark for author-vs-quoted claim separation and source ownership in authentic news argumentation.

citation: Pareti, O'Keefe et al. lineage; ACL LREC 2020
title: RiQuA: A Corpus of Rich Quotation Annotation for English
authors: authors as listed in scholarly PDF; exact author list not retyped because page extraction was partial
task_description: Annotate rich reported speech and quotation events, including direct/indirect speech, cues, speakers, and addressees where applicable.
inputs: English text across news and other genres as described in the paper; exact corpus composition requires full PDF follow-up
outputs_or_labels: Quotation/report spans, speech-event cue, speaker, listener/addressee, quotation type and coreference-related roles
pipeline_gap_filled: reported speech; speaker ownership; addressee-aware discourse structure
artifact_access_status: paper PDF search result accessible; dataset public availability not verified
evidence_basis: Search result from the scholarly PDF explicitly describes RiQuA as a rich quotation annotation corpus and contrasts it with PDTB, STOP, and RWG; retained evidence names cue, speaker, listener/addressee and direct/indirect categories.
limitations: Author list, artifact URL, counts, and license were not fully recoverable in this run; treat as a lead requiring verification before operational adoption.
why_relevant: Potentially the best reported-speech benchmark for ownership plus interlocutor structure, but evidence is incomplete.

title: DirectQuote: A Dataset for Direct Quotation Extraction and Attribution in News Articles
task_description: Jointly extract direct-quotation spans from news paragraphs and attribute each quotation to its original speaker.
outputs_or_labels: 10,279 manually annotated direct quotations and corresponding speakers; speakers linkable to Wikidata; end-to-end baselines
pipeline_gap_filled: reported speech; source ownership; entity-linked attribution
artifact_access_status: official GitHub repository named in paper; data access not independently tested
evidence_basis: ACL PDF search result gives counts, task, Wikidata linking, and repository URL; arXiv abstract corroborates corpus purpose and manual annotation.
limitations: Direct quotations only; does not cover indirect quotation, private states, nested attribution, or author stance outside quoted speech.
why_relevant: High-value news benchmark for quote extraction plus speaker attribution, with entity linking useful for provenance graphs.

title: The Project Dialogism Novel Corpus: A Dataset for Quotation Attribution in Literary Texts
authors: Krishnapriya Vishnubhotla; Adam Hammond; Graeme Hirst
task_description: Attribute quotations in full-length English novels to speakers and addressees, with quotation type, referring expression, and character mentions.
outputs_or_labels: 35,978 quotations; speaker, addressee(s), quotation type, referring expression, and within-quote character mentions
pipeline_gap_filled: reported speech; implicit/anaphoric ownership; addressee and coreference structure
artifact_access_status: official GitHub repository linked from project page; raw texts sourced from Project Gutenberg
license_status: dataset license not verified; source texts have upstream Project Gutenberg terms
evidence_basis: ACL/arXiv scholarly evidence verifies 22 novels, 35,978 quotations, and annotation fields; official project page verifies repository and manual annotation.
limitations: Literary fiction rather than scholarly/argumentative prose; speaker labels are character ownership, not author-vs-cited-source stance.
why_relevant: Useful control and transfer benchmark for difficult implicit/anaphoric quote ownership and coreference.

title: Who Said What: Formalization and Benchmarks for the Task of Quote Attribution
authors: Wenjie Zhong; Jason Naradowsky; Hiroya Takamura; Ichiro Kobayashi; Yusuke Miyao
artifact_url: datasets listed in paper; exact artifact endpoint not verified
task_description: Formalize quote attribution and benchmark supervised, QA, and LLM systems across all available English and Chinese datasets.
inputs: Seven existing quote-attribution datasets: four English and three Chinese; document-plus-quote contexts
outputs_or_labels: Speaker identity selected/linked from document; comparable benchmark results and error analysis
pipeline_gap_filled: reported speech; standardized evaluation of ownership attribution
artifact_access_status: paper open; underlying datasets are existing resources with heterogeneous access
license_status: varies by underlying dataset; not unified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL page/search result verifies task formalization, seven datasets, bilingual coverage, and exhaustive model benchmark.
limitations: Benchmark aggregates existing datasets rather than introducing one unified annotation resource; literary/news domains and label schemas differ.
why_relevant: Important evaluation harness for comparing claim-ownership models and exposing dataset/version effects.

title: A Two-stage Sieve Approach for Quote Attribution
authors: Grace Muzny; Michael Fang; Angel X. Chang; Dan Jurafsky
artifact_url: QuoteLi3 artifact endpoint not independently verified
task_description: Link quote spans to speaker mentions and then resolve mentions to speaker entities in literary text.
inputs: Three novels: Pride and Prejudice, Emma, The Steppe
outputs_or_labels: 3,103 quotes with quote-mention and quote-speaker/entity labels; >6,000 annotations including >3,000 newly annotated
artifact_access_status: paper open; artifact URL not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL PDF search result explicitly states QuoteLi3 dataset, three novels, mention/entity labels, and 6,206 labels.
limitations: Literary rather than argumentative text; limited number of novels and no source/cue/content attribution relation beyond quoted speech.
why_relevant: Compact, inspectable benchmark for separating textual referring expressions from the underlying speaker entity.

citation: Newell et al. (2018) and Pareti (2016) benchmark family
title: PARC3–PolNeAR Attribution Extraction Family
authors: Silvia Pareti; Edward Newell; Drew Margolin; Derek Ruths
task_description: Cross-resource evaluation of attribution extraction with source/cue/content roles, including nested/overlapping versus univocal annotations.
inputs: News text from PDTB/WSJ and political-news articles
outputs_or_labels: Comparable source/cue/content role inventories; attribution-level agreement and token-level labels
pipeline_gap_filled: benchmark harmonization for author-vs-quoted claim separation and disagreement attribution
artifact_access_status: PolNeAR repository open; PARC3 paper says research availability; unified conversion not provided
evidence_basis: Opened ACL pages verify PARC3's source/cue/content scheme and PolNeAR's scholarly identity; official PolNeAR repository documents contrasts with PARC3 and dataset structure.
limitations: Not a single benchmark release; schema mismatch and different corpora require explicit normalization before joint use.
why_relevant: Directly informs a benchmark design that preserves disagreement, nesting, source ownership, and authorial stance rather than collapsing all quotes to speaker IDs.

citation: Aharoni et al. (2014), Argumentation Mining Workshop
title: A Benchmark Dataset for Automatic Detection of Claims and Evidence in the Context of Controversial Topics
authors: Ehud Aharoni; Anatoly Polnarov; Tamar Lavee; Daniel Hershcovich; Ran Levy; Ruty Rinott; Dan Gutfreund; Noam Slonim
task_description: Detect claims and evidence in controversial-topic text; evaluate argument-mining extraction without explicit source ownership labels.
outputs_or_labels: Claim/evidence annotations; exact label inventory and size require paper-level follow-up
pipeline_gap_filled: argument structure control; evidence linkage without attribution ownership
artifact_access_status: paper open; artifact download via ACL PDF/page
license_status: materials pre-2016 listed by ACL as CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
evidence_basis: ACL metadata/search result verifies benchmark identity, task, venue, and access/license statement.
limitations: Does not identify who owns each claim or distinguish author from quoted/disagreed source; included as adjacent control only.
why_relevant: Provides the argument-extraction side needed to pair attribution-aware source roles with claim/evidence relations.
